findings.title: POST /api/payment/request has no order-status guard — a payment link can be minted for an already-paid/cancelled order
findings.suggested_fix: Only allow payment initiation when order.status === 'pending_payment' (return 400 otherwise) before calling paymentRouter.requestPaymentWithFailover and before overwriting `authority`.

findings.title: markOrderPaid double-credits VIP points under concurrent verify callbacks on PostgreSQL
findings.suggested_fix: On PG (READ COMMITTED) two concurrent /verify callbacks can both read status='pending_payment' and both credit points. Make the transition atomic: UPDATE orders SET status='processing' WHERE id=? AND status='pending_payment' RETURNING, and only credit points when a row was returned (same pattern as the oversell fix in orders.ts).

findings.title: User cancel: check-then-act status guard is not atomic — concurrent double-cancel double-restocks and double-refunds on PG
findings.suggested_fix: Perform the status flip first with an atomic predicate: UPDATE orders SET status='cancelled' WHERE id=? AND status IN ('pending_payment','processing') RETURNING; if no row, abort. Then restock/refund once. Same defect exists in the cancel branch of PUT /api/admin/orders/:id/status (admin.ts:526-550).

findings.title: Coupon usage cap is TOCTOU on PostgreSQL — concurrent orders can exceed usageLimit
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same atomic-predicate pattern used for stock: UPDATE coupons SET used_count = used_count + 1 WHERE code = ? AND (usage_limit IS NULL OR used_count < usage_limit) RETURNING code; if 0 rows, reject the coupon. The read-only check at line 154 is racy on PG.

findings.title: Stock/price changes never bust the `product:<id>` detail cache — invalidate('products') does not match 'product:<id>' keys
findings.suggested_fix: 'products' is not a substring of 'product:5', so GET /api/products/:id keeps serving stale stockQuantity/price for up to 60s after an order, cancellation, or admin product edit. Invalidate('product:') (prefix) or call appCache.invalidate() with no pattern for product mutations.

findings.title: PUT /api/cart/:id accepts any quantity — max-10 and stock guards are not enforced on update
findings.suggested_fix: Validate 1 <= quantity <= 10 and quantity <= product.stockQuantity (as POST / does). Currently a client can set quantity=999999; the invariant is only rescued later by the order-transaction stock guard.

findings.title: VIP clawback can drive vipPoints negative
findings.suggested_fix: If an admin adjusted the user's points (PUT /api/admin/users/:id/points sets an absolute value) after the order was credited, the clawback subtracts from a balance that may not contain those points, producing a negative vip_points. Clamp with SQL: set vipPoints = MAX(0, vipPoints - X) or guard with vipPoints >= X.

findings.title: Empty catch blocks silently swallow errors in the Bale bot
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum log the swallowed error (console.warn with the method/context); silent catches hide broken notification/fallback paths.

findings.title: No dedicated rate limiter on POST /api/orders, POST /api/payment/request, /api/auth/refresh — only the general 600/15min cap
findings.suggested_fix: POST /api/payment/request hammers external bank gateways on each call and /api/auth/refresh is an unauthenticated token-oracle endpoint; give both a strict limiter (e.g. 10-20/min/IP), matching the authLimiter pattern.

findings.title: GET /api/admin/analytics loads every order+items, every user and every product into JS memory
findings.suggested_fix: Category sales and top-selling products are expressible as SQL GROUP BY joins over order_items; the sales trend can filter orders to the 14-day window instead of scanning all history. Same full-table pattern remains in GET /api/admin/orders when page/limit are omitted (admin.ts:500-505).

findings.title: Order creation inserts order items and updates stock one row at a time inside the transaction
findings.suggested_fix: Batch-insert orderItems with a single tx.insert().values(items[]). Keep the per-item guarded UPDATE for the row-count oversell assert, but consider batching the inserts; minor latency win per order, matters most on PG round-trips.

findings.title: PUT /api/users/me can take an already-registered phone — unique-constraint violation surfaces as a generic 500
findings.suggested_fix: Pre-check `phone` uniqueness (or catch the constraint error and return 400 with a Persian message). A failed unique index currently yields a generic 500 and the profile update is silently lost.

findings.title: Coupon validation response leaks internal usage data via raw row
findings.suggested_fix: `coupon` is the raw DB row including usedCount/usageLimit/expiresAt internals. Return only {code,label,percent,amount,minTotal} plus computed discount/finalTotal.
